chapter_title: Day 1: Istanbul, a City on Two Continents
learning_objective: The learner will classify twelve Istanbul places by the shore they stand on (the historic peninsula, Galata, or the Asian shore), classifying at least 10 of 12 correctly on the first attempt.

**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify twelve Istanbul places by the shore they stand on (the historic peninsula, Galata, or the Asian shore), classifying at least 10 of 12 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** strait, Bosphorus Strait, historic peninsula, Galata, Asian shore, Golden Horn (all defined in the section "The Bosphorus Strait" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the twelve places, the learner commits to one of three shores before the place's marker is revealed on the map. A classification is correct when it matches the Correct shore column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt. Panning the map and opening place infoboxes after the quiz is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) All of Istanbul is in Europe. (2) The Golden Horn is part of the Bosphorus, so Galata is in Asia. (3) The old Greek city of Byzantium stood where the modern city center (Taksim) is. (4) The walls of Constantinople run along the Bosphorus. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying places by shore makes the learner build a mental model of the city's three parts and the two bodies of water that divide them. Committing to a shore before the marker appears is a prediction, and the reveal on the real map corrects the model immediately. **Content:** The map shows the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the northern edge of the Sea of Marmara, with three labeled regions: Historic peninsula (European side, south of the Golden Horn), Galata (European side, north of the Golden Horn), Asian shore (east of the Bosphorus). Region labels are shown; place markers are hidden until each is answered. | # | Place | Latitude | Longitude | Correct shore | Infobox text (shown after answering) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Sarayburnu (Seraglio Point) | 41.0157 | 28.9850 | Historic peninsula | The tip of the peninsula, where Greek Byzantium stood and Topkapı Palace stands now. | | 2 | Hagia Sophia | 41.0086 | 28.9802 | Historic peninsula | Built 537 as a cathedral; Day 2's chapter. | | 3 | Column of Constantine (Çemberlitaş) | 41.0084 | 28.9711 | Historic peninsula | Raised for the dedication of Constantinople in 330; still standing on Divan Yolu. | | 4 | Golden Gate (Yedikule) | 40.9935 | 28.9223 | Historic peninsula | The ceremonial entrance at the southern end of the Theodosian land walls. | | 5 | Edirnekapı (Gate of Adrianople) | 41.0310 | 28.9370 | Historic peninsula | A gate of the land walls; Mehmed II rode in near here on May 29, 1453. | | 6 | Fatih Mosque | 41.0195 | 28.9497 | Historic peninsula | Built by Mehmed II on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles, where Constantine was buried. | | 7 | Eminönü ferry piers | 41.0170 | 28.9740 | Historic peninsula | The balık ekmek boats and the ferries to Asia leave from here. | | 8 | Galata Tower | 41.0256 | 28.9741 | Galata | Built by the Genoese in 1348; the sunset view over the Golden Horn. | | 9 | Rumeli Hisarı | 41.0846 | 29.0563 | Galata | Mehmed II's 1452 fortress at the narrows. It stands on the European shore north of Galata; for this quiz, all of the European side north of the Golden Horn counts as Galata. | | 10 | Kadıköy ferry pier | 40.9925 | 29.0240 | Asian shore | Ancient Chalcedon, "the city of the blind." | | 11 | Üsküdar | 41.0260 | 29.0150 | Asian shore | Ancient Chrysopolis, where Constantine defeated Licinius in 324. | | 12 | Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) | 41.0211 | 29.0041 | Asian shore | A small tower on an islet just off the Asian shore, opposite the peninsula. | **Provenance:** Coordinates are approximate and taken from OpenStreetMap; the generator should verify each against OpenStreetMap before building and correct any that are off by more than 200 m. The infobox facts come from this chapter's sections "The Bosphorus Strait," "Byzantium," "Constantine the Great," "The Theodosian Walls," "Mehmed the Conqueror" and "The Golden Horn." **Rules:** Each place has exactly one correct shore. For this quiz, the European shore north of the Golden Horn, including Rumeli Hisarı, counts as Galata; the infobox for place 9 says so. Places are asked in the fixed order listed. A place counts as correct only on the learner's first answer. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the map with the three regions labeled and the prompt for place 1. 2. The learner chooses a shore. The place's marker appears at its true location, the correct shore is shown, and the infobox opens. 3. The learner continues through all twelve places. 4. After place 12, every marker is shown together and the learner can open any infobox and pan the map. 5. The learner should notice that everything Byzantine and early Ottoman (places 1 to 7) is on the historic peninsula, while the foreign merchants' tower and the Asian-side towns sit across water from it. **Feedback:** Twelve places, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Right: is on the ." plus the infobox text. Incorrect: "Not quite: is on the ." plus the infobox text; for place 8 add "The Golden Horn separates Galata from the old city, but both are in Europe." A running score "Shores correct: n of 12" is shown. At the end: "10 or more: you know your way around" or "Fewer than 10: look again at where the Golden Horn meets the Bosphorus, then try again." A Restart button clears answers and hides the markers. **Starting State:** The map centered on the meeting of the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn, the three regions labeled, no markers, and the question "Sarayburnu (Seraglio Point): which shore?" **Chapter Anchors:** The Bosphorus is about 31 km long and between about 700 m and 3.7 km wide. The ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy takes about twenty minutes. Galata Tower, 1348. Rumeli Hisarı, 1452. Column of Constantine, 330. Chalcedon is "the city of the blind."
